articles.title: Haydock tips: Big Mojo fancied to retain Sprint Cup crown
articles.summary: Ahead of another busy Saturday of action, Kate Tracey is joined on the Weekend Winners panel by Callum Helliwell and Declan Rix; in this week's episode, the team take aim at Haydock, paying particular attention to the feature Sprint Cup
articles.body:
Eight runners are set to go in challenging conditions, with the ground expected to be heavy for this six-furlong dash.

Almeraq heads the market as he aims to bounce back from disappointment in the July Cup, while Wathnan duo Kind Of Blue and Paborus also take their chance. Marvelman and Coppull represent Andrew Balding and Clive Cox respectively, and last year's winner Big Mojo returns to defend his crown.

"I'm with the favourite Almeraq . He's a wonderful horse who I think deserves an awful lot of credit after that horror fall he took at York - it was a proper mother-and-a-father fall. To come back and win on his first start in the Cathedral Stakes, it was like someone had said a prayer for him.

"Not only did he win the Cathedral, he then went to Royal Ascot and won the QEII Jubilee. Tom Marquand said he felt a bit claustrophobic, but I love that he sustains his runs and has a good attitude.

"He has a good, strong shoulder and I think he'll handle the ground. He's got plenty of form in his career on soft, whether he'll handle heavy ground - we'll see. I think you can completely forgive him the July Cup form as it was his first time going down a hill and the field broke, leaving him caught on a wing. He ran too keen, got no cover and the ground was too quick for him.

"If he runs like any of the horses the William Haggas team ran at Haydock on Thursday, he's going to go very close as they're in great order."

"I absolutely love Marvelman in this - bring on the rain! I want it to be an absolute bog by the time Marvelman gets there. We're going to have another day of racing before then!

In the Park Stakes on September 13 last year it was a great birthday present for Callum, as it he absolutely gagged up.

He ran a mighty race last time, having them all off it from a long way home when finishing third in top-class company. Keep the rain coming!"

"I'm going to be with Big Mojo to repeat the feat from last year. I thought 9/1 was a fair price - although not as big as last year when he took full advantage of the draw bias. He has a similar draw this time so I'm hoping it will come to the fore.

Three runs ago he finished eight at Royal Ascot in the Group 1 King Charles III Stakes, not being beaten far whatsoever. Admittedly he was in the right group that day when the bias came to the fore and improved from his reappearance at York.

The July Cup was no good for him, he looked a nightmare that day. He was so keen and was hanging but it was much more like it at the Curragh last time, getting back to winning ways in a Group 3. Hopefully that's the confidence booster he needs.

Watch Weekend Winners in full on the At The Races YouTube channel…

articles.title: Daryz warms up for Arc with dominant display in Prix Foy
articles.summary: Daryz was given the perfect rehearsal ahead of his bid to retain his crown in the Prix de l'Arc de Triomphe with a smooth success in the Prix Foy at Parislongchamp
articles.body:
Francis-Henri Graffard's charge made the perfect start to his four-year-old campaign by winning two more Group Ones at his beloved ParisLongchamp, with a comeback victory in the Prix Ganay followed by a runaway triumph in the Prix Aga Khan IV.

He could only finish third when sent across the Channel for the Prince of Wales's Stakes at Royal Ascot in June, but with connections feeling they had viable excuses for that below-par run, the son of Sea The Stars was expected to regain winning ways back on home turf.

On paper his task was not entirely straightforward, with George Scott's 10-length Coronation Cup winner and fellow Arc aspirant Bay City Roller among his three rivals, and as expected the latter was sent straight to the front by Oisin Murphy in an attempt to draw the sting out of Daryz's exceptional finishing kick.

But Mickael Barzalona always looked ultra-confident in the saddle aboard the red-hot favourite, who cruised alongside Bay City Roller a furlong out and only had to be pushed out hands and heels to win by a length and three-quarters.

"I couldn't be happier with the trial he had today. We got a good lead and luckily Oisin made the pace a little bit harder at the top of the hill, so the horse was really travelling nicely," Graffard told Sky Sports Racing.

"For me as a trainer it was the best preparation I could have for the horse. He will come on a lot for that, I left plenty in him, so he should be spot-on for four weeks' time."

Scott too was delighted with the performance of the runner-up and is hoping for rain in Paris ahead of a rematch with Daryz in Europe's premier middle-distance contest on October 4.

He said: "Oisin was very happy with him and we'll be hoping for a different set of circumstances in a month's time.

"We know that this horse has a high level of form on ground like this, but when it rains he's a different animal.

"He came here and travelled well, went through the race very well and got beaten by a better horse on the day. In four weeks' time that might be the case (again), but it might not, so we'll see.

"I think he's the best version of himself now. The winner might be as well, but in four weeks' time it's going to be completely different.

"He's going to be an underdog coming back, of course he is - Daryz is a champion and he is unbelievable around here. It was all perfect for him today and set up great, but I was very happy with our horse, Oisin was most happy, so we're looking forward to it."

Avec Toi made to work hard to stay unbeaten in Prix la Rochette

Hot favourite Avec Toi was made to pull out all the stops to maintain his unbeaten record in the Qatar Prix la Rochette at ParisLongchamp.

Christopher Head's colt had been hugely impressive in winning his first three starts and was long odds-on to make it four from four in this Group Three contest.

Imperial Strike, winner of his two previous starts for Andre and Lavinia Fabre, made a real race of it and there was little to choose between the pair in the dying strides, but Avec Toi was a short head in front at the line.

A likely rematch between the front two will take place in the Prix Jean-Luc Lagardere in four weeks' time.

Head told Sky Sports Racing: "It was a very nice race with five nice horses. I respected Imperial Strike from the beginning, so I'm very happy our horse won the race and we discovered there's a very nice horse to beat next time too!

"He's a very nice horse and he's done a great job today. It was a pretty tactical race and we are all happy.

"There is a lot to do between the two races and I'm very happy with that."

Ed Bethell's British raider Rogue Passion flashed home to claim Group Two honours in the Qatar Prix d'Aumale.

The Sioux Nation filly faced a significant step up in class having opened her account at the third time of asking at Carlisle three weeks ago.

Francis-Henri Graffard's Amusingly looked likely to win comfortably after travelling powerfully into the lead under Colin Keane, but Rossa Ryan produced Rogue Passion with a well-timed challenge to get up and claim victory.

Bethell told the Press Association: "We were hoping that she'd run a big race, she's a very nice filly who I've got a lot of time for.

"Obviously you don't know what you're taking on with the French horses, but she quickened up like a decent filly over the mile there and we're delighted."

When asked whether she would return to Paris for the Prix Marcel Boussac next month, the trainer added: "It's a conversation that needs to be had with the guys at Rogues Gallery (owners) because she needs to be supplemented if we're going to do it.

"We'll let the dust settle today, enjoy it and have the conversation in a few days' time. She's got options, but now she's a Group Two winner we want to try and get a Group One if we can.

"Today definitely was not unexpected. She's always shown she's a nice filly and it's a huge credit to the Rogues Gallery and Henry Lascelles who bought her."

articles.title: Spanish GP: Kimi Antonelli edges Ferrari in Madrid practice as Arvid Lindblad suffers first F1 crash at challenging Madring circuit
articles.summary: Kimi Antonelli fastest from Ferrari's Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton in Practice Two; Arvid Lindblad first F1 driver to crash at new Madrid track; watch Spanish GP Qualifying from the all-new Madring circuit live on Sky Sports F1 at 3pm on Saturday
articles.body:
After being outpaced by his Mercedes team-mate George Russell in the day's first session, Antonelli produced a quicker time of 1:33.662 in Practice Two to edge out Ferrari duo Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton by little more than a tenth of a second.

The timesheet was further evidence of Antonelli's sky-high confidence, which was elevated by a stunning victory at the Italian Grand Prix last weekend as he won his home race from 19th on the grid to move 66 points clear of Russell at the top of the standings with 10 rounds of the 2026 season remaining.

On the evidence of Friday's sessions, Mercedes and Ferrari are closely matched and could deliver an exciting pole contest in qualifying on Saturday, with huge excitement in the Spanish capital as F1 returns to the city for the first time since 1981.

Many had predicted a high number of red flags on Friday - and throughout the rest of the weekend - due to the tight and punishing nature of a circuit that the field have never raced at before.

While there were several crashes and red flags in Friday's F2 and F3 sessions, the F1 drivers showed their excellence to avoid any major incidents in first practice, but it was Lindblad who came unstuck just beyond the halfway point of Practice Two.

The 19-year-old was driving impressively and had just elevated himself to fourth when he pushed too hard on his next flying lap, losing control at Turn 13 and spinning into the barrier at high speed.

Lindblad said: "It's not an easy track. We are all pushing to find the limits. It's new for all of us. Just made a bit of a mistake and overdid it in Turn 13. A shame. I apologise to the mechanics and the team. It's extra work for them tonight.

"But looking at the big picture, it's been a good day. We are very fast. I was running P4 on merit and was only two tenths from P1 which is really strong.

"A lot of confidence in the team going into tomorrow. I'm just focused on resetting and trying to block it out and taking all the good learnings."

A delay of just over 10 minutes put an end to the qualifying simulations that had been taking place at that stage, securing Antonelli's position at the top of the timesheet.

Russell was fifth after appearing to struggle to optimise his setup, but still managed to edge out Red Bull's Max Verstappen and McLaren's Oscar Piastri.

"It was fun to drive the track for the first time," Russell said. "It's always a great experience driving a new circuit.

"FP1 was a strong session. FP2 we made some setup changes which weren't quite as good, so we will probably revert back on that. So far so good."

Reigning world champion Lando Norris was unable to set a time after a gearbox failure took him out of the session after just two laps.

McLaren were expected to be competitive in Madrid given Norris had claimed back-to-back victories before Antonelli's win in Monza, but there was little evidence of that on Friday.

While Norris has generally been quicker than Piastri recently, losing an entire session at a new circuit will put the Brit on the back foot going into Saturday.

articles.title: Azerbaijan GP: McLaren predict four-way battle for victory with rivals in Baku after confirming more upgrades to MCL40
articles.summary: McLaren have shown strong recent form with Lando Norris claiming three pole positions and two race victories across the last four rounds; watch every session of the Azerbaijan GP from Thursday live on Sky Sports F1, with the race on Saturday at 12pm
articles.body:
After failing to claim a victory in the first 10 grands prix of the season, the reigning constructors' champions have come into form, with Lando Norris claiming three pole positions at the last four races and only being denied a third win by the unfortunate timing of a virtual safety car last time out in Madrid.

McLaren have once more exhibited strength in development, with regular upgrades brought to the MCL40 having played a significant part in catapulting them back into contention for victories.

The team's official preview for this weekend's race in Baku, which takes place on Saturday rather than the usual Sunday slot, revealed there will be new parts, and that their rotating 'H-Wing' will return to the car after not being used in Madrid.

"As part of the team's continued journey throughout the 2026 season, the team will bring to Baku a set of upgrades aimed to improve the aerodynamic performance of the MCL40," the team said.

"Additionally the H-Wing, that debuted in Monza, will be back in action on a track where the drag reduction can be a factor.

"As has been the approach in previous races this season, all new parts will be evaluated throughout practice before the team makes final decisions regarding the MCL40's Qualifying and Grand Prix setup for the weekend."

McLaren chief technical officer and chief designer Rob Marshall explained the team are keen to continue their development push despite their title hopes being extremely thin, with Kimi Antonelli dominating the Drivers' Championship and his Mercedes team well clear in the constructors' standings.

"With regulatory continuity into next season and the competition at the front so close, our motivation to keep developing the car remains high," Marshall said.

"We must balance that with work on next year's car, but our immediate focus is on delivering more performance and fighting for more victories in 2026, while carrying forward everything we learn."

The Baku circuit, which features the longest straight on the F1 calendar alongside several slow corners, creates a challenge that Marshall expects to create entertaining competition between the top teams.

"Baku will provide another valuable test of the MCL40 across a very different range of characteristics," Marshall added.

"Energy management and deployment will be particularly important, as will tyre and brake management with the cars arriving at Turn 1 after the long straight with these areas relatively cold.

"Operationally, there is very little margin for error on a tight street circuit. A small mistake can lead to significant repairs, lost track time and resources being diverted away from performance, so confidence, precision and disciplined execution will be essential throughout the weekend.

"We expect any of the top four teams to be capable of winning in Baku, with the chasing pack also getting closer, and we hope to be firmly in the fight at the front."

articles.title: Llegan carreras de F1 más cortas
articles.standfirst: La Comisión de la F1 da luz verde a varios cambios ya para 2027
articles.summary: La Comisión de la F1 da luz verde a varios cambios ya para 2027
articles.body: La Comisión de la F1, reunida en Londres por tercera vez esta temporada y presidida por Nicolas Tombazis, su responsable técnico, y por Stefano Domenicali, su CEO, ha acordado unos cambios de los que se habían hablado, pero que, ahora, reciben luz verde definitiva. El más llamativo es que las carreras de F1 serán más cortas a partir de 2027. Se ha establecido que la distancia de carrera pase de los actuales 305 kilómetros a sólo 290 kilómetros el curso venidero. Según la FIA, esto supondrá una reducción "de dos o tres vueltas" en función del circuito. La causa de esta disminución se encuentra en el pacto al que llegaron los equipos, la FIA y la F1 respecto a los cambios que se realizarán en las unidades de potencia para 2027 y 2028. Poco a poco la parte de combustible irá ganando terreno a la eléctrica, hasta llegar al 60 por ciento frente al 40 en 2028. Esto hace que la parte térmica necesite más combustible. Se barajó poner depósitos más grandes, pero eso aumentaría el peso de unos monoplazas ya muy pesados, con lo que se decidió reducir las carreras. Otra variación aprobada es la referida a las interrupciones de una carrera por lluvia, accidente u otras circunstancias. Ahora, se fijará una hora límite, de forma anticipada y no habrá que esperar tres horas, como era hasta ahora. Eso sí, se mantiene que debe haber un máximo de dos horas seguidas de carrera. La Comisión sigue esa línea al permitir que los entrenamientos también se puedan alargar, aunque, en este caso, no se especifica ni cómo ni cuánto. Además, y de acuerdo con el dictamen de la comisión técnica, se decidió que ya no será necesaria una homologación de las cajas de cambio en 2027. Según la FIA, así se podrá "preservar la libertad de desarrollo de los proveedores".

articles.title: Formula 1 reduces maximum distance of races by 15km among changes for 2027
articles.summary: F1 announces the maximum race distance for grands prix will be reduced by 15km from 305km to 290km for the 2027 season.
articles.body:
Formula 1 has announced the maximum race distance for grands prix will be reduced by 15km from 305km (189.5 miles) to 290km (180.2 miles) for the 2027 season.

Grands prix are limited to a maximum of two hours of racing, but when there are interruptions caused by rain or accidents, a "hard stop time" will replace the current maximum three-hour duration to finish the event.

This will allow for greater flexibility to complete disrupted races.

A statement from governing body the FIA said: "These changes were introduced to ensure that the spectators have the best possible chance to enjoy a full race if disruptions occur."

The hard stop time will vary from race to race, depending on local conditions.

At night races, for example, there will be more flexibility to allow the race to run later than at a daytime race when there is a relatively early sunset.

The reduction in race distance has been introduced because the ratio of internal combustion to electrical power is changing from 53-47 this year to 58-42 next year, before becoming 60-40 in 2028.

This means that the cars will use more fuel, and that became a concern when it emerged that some teams wanted to carry their chassis over into next year to save money.

As the fuel tank is within the chassis and therefore its size could not be changed, this meant those teams might not have been able to finish grands prix with their existing fuel tanks.

Another change agreed at a meeting of the F1 Commission, a rule-making body composed of the teams, the FIA and commercial rights holder F1, was to introduce "greater flexibility to extend free practice sessions should they be interrupted".

Under current rules, the clock does not stop in practice sessions in the event of a red flag caused by an incident, unlike in qualifying and races when the competition is suspended.

images.caption: Image caption, New rules will cover F1 races delayed or disrupted by rain or incidents from 2027

articles.title: F1 Grand Prix distances set to be reduced for 2027 season along with introduction of 'hard stop' time on race days
articles.summary: Grand Prix distances will be reduced from 305km to 290km in 2027; the change is required due to the alteration of technical regulations for next season; watch every session of the Azerbaijan GP from Thursday live on Sky Sports F1, with the race on Saturday at 12pm
articles.body:
At a meeting of the F1 Commission in London on Monday, the sport's decision makers agreed to reduce Grand Prix distances from 305km to 290km, which corresponds to a reduction of two to three laps depending on the circuit.

The change is being made because fuel flow rates are being increased next season as part of measures the FIA are introducing to optimise the all-new regulations brought in at the start of 2026.

The FIA said: "In line with the refinements to the Power Unit regulations to be introduced in 2027 on fuel flow, a reduction in the total race distance from 305km to 290km was approved, corresponding to a reduction of two or three laps."

The decision must be approved by the World Motor Sport Council, but that is expected to be a formality.

The FIA also announced slight changes to protocols around races disrupted by rain or other factors, with a three-hour limit (including interruptions) from race to start to finish removed, but a "hard stop" time for the end of any racing activity to be introduced.

A limit of two hours of actual racing remains, with those decisions taken "to ensure that the spectators have the best possible chance to enjoy a full race if disruptions occur."

It was also confirmed that there will be "greater flexibility to extend Free Practice sessions should they be interrupted."

The current rules only allow for practice sessions to be extended on Sprint weekends, but such measures may now also be available on a regular schedule.
